### Why Should I Be Excited About Leviticus?
Author: Lysa TerKeurst
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/why-should-i-be-excited-about-leviticus-encouragement-for-today-february-18-2016.html
Passage: Leviticus 1:3
Points:
- Ancient sacrificial rituals reveal key heart attitudes for following God today.
- God does not demand everything we possess, but invites us to gratefully return a portion.
- Believers are called to offer God their very best time, thoughts, and energy rather than leftovers.
- Presenting the offering at the entrance signifies giving God the first priority in everyday life.

### In Order
Author: Daily Disciples Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-disciples/daily-disciples-devotional-feb-7-2009-11599163.html
Passage: Leviticus 1:7
Points:
- God's instruction to arrange altar wood carefully reveals His intentional focus on order.
- Bringing biblical order to home life and schedules fosters peace and contentment.
- Believers are challenged to identify disorder and seek God's help to align their priorities.
- Dedicating the first fruits of each day to the Lord allows Him to guide the rest of it.

### The Burnt Offering
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier.org
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/burnt-offering
Passage: Leviticus 1:1-17
Points:
- Burnt offerings served as propitiation to satisfy God's holy wrath and preserve covenant fellowship.
- The requirement of an entire burnt animal underscored the serious costliness of true worship.
- Laying hands upon the animal's head signified the transfer and imputation of sin onto a substitute.
- The Old Covenant sacrifices pointed ahead to Christ's ultimate substitutionary death on the cross.

### Bible Pathways - February 1, 2006
Author: Dr. John A. Hash
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-february-1-2006-1375714.html
Passage: Leviticus 1:2-4
Points:
- The voluntary burnt offering signified complete personal submission to the Lord without selfish motives.
- God graciously accepted different tiers of animals according to each person's financial situation.
- Pressing hands upon the animal represented the transfer of guilt from sinner to innocent substitute.
- The shed blood on the altar foreshadowed the redeeming sacrifice of Jesus Christ.
